extracted.intended_audience: Catholic catechism students, parents, and instructors (laypeople preparing for or administering sacraments)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructional rules and standards for administering and receiving the Catholic sacraments of Baptism, Confirmation, and Penance, including required materials, exact formulas, procedural steps, eligibility, spiritual preparation, and the meaning of rites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid matter and words for Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: Baptism requires the use of clean water and the precise verbal formula for validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ordinary clean water (warm or cold); no other liquid will do. The same person must both pour the water and pronounce the words; it is invalid if one person pours and another says the words. Say every one of the exact words: "I baptize thee in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." Variants such as "I baptize thee in the name of God," "I baptize thee in the name of the Blessed Trinity," or omitting "I baptize thee" (e.g. saying only "In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost") are not valid. Pour the water so that it touches the skin (pour on the head); do not merely sprinkle or pour on the hair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not repeat a valid Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: Once Baptism has been validly administered, it must not be repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After careful administration, never under any circumstance repeat the Baptism on the same person. Attempting to baptize more than once when one knows Baptism can be given only once is a sin. Be calm and careful especially in emergency (danger-of-death) situations to ensure validity rather than repeating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private (emergency) vs solemn Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between private (emergency) baptism and solemn baptism with ceremonies in church, and post-emergency obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private Baptism: pouring water and pronouncing the words without the other church ceremonies; used in necessity (e.g., in a private house). Sponsors are not necessary in private Baptism. Persons baptized privately should be brought to the church afterwards to receive the rest of the ceremonies (solemn Baptism) if possible. Solemn Baptism: performed in church with full ceremonies and symbolic rites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required preparations and materials for solemn Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: List of items that must be prepared for the solemn (church) baptism ceremony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare holy oils, a little salt, a small pitcher or similar to pour water from, a vessel to receive water when poured, some cotton, two stoles (one white and one purple), towels, a white cloth (garment), a candle, and a candlestick. Each item has symbolic significance (see ceremony/significance rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial steps and symbolic meanings in solemn Baptism
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of ceremonial actions during solemn Baptism and the symbolic meaning of each element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical steps: the priest asks "What do you ask of the Church of God?" (godparents answer "Faith"); priest exhorts and breathes three times to bid the evil spirit depart; prayer; placing a little salt into the mouth (signifies wisdom that Faith gives); placement of the stole over the child (signifies being led into the Church); recitation of the Creed and Our Father (for adult candidates); spittle applied to ears/nose (evokes Christ's healing gestures); anointing with holy oil on breast and back; profession of faith; baptizing (pouring water with formula); anointing head with chrism; white cloth/garment placed to signify purity and Resurrection; a lighted candle placed in the hand to signify the light of faith; frequent signing with the Sign of the Cross to recall salvation by the Cross; stole to show Church protection; anointing as sign of being freed from sins and strengthened. The baptistery is by the door to show that without Baptism one is outside the Church.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baptism types and sufficiency (water, desire, blood)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three kinds of Baptism—of water, of desire, and of blood—and each has a precise definition and conditions for producing the effects of Baptism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baptism of water: given by pouring water on the head while saying the baptismal formula. Baptism of desire: an ardent wish to receive Baptism and to do what God ordains, applicable when one cannot actually receive water Baptism (e.g., no one to baptize). Baptism of blood (martyrdom): received by those put to death for the faith before receiving water Baptism. Baptism of desire or blood is sufficient to produce the effects of Baptism if it is impossible to receive Baptism of water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency (necessity) baptism rules and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Special cautions when baptizing in cases of necessity or danger of death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful and calm; use clean water and nothing else; the same person must both pour and say the words simultaneously; ensure water touches the skin and pouring (not sprinkling). Parents should not baptize their own children if another valid baptizer is present. Remember sponsors are not necessary in private Baptism. After emergency baptism, follow up in church to complete rites if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors / godparents: purpose, obligations, and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors are given to promise in the child's name, instruct the child if parents neglect, and they form a spiritual relationship with the child; strict eligibility criteria apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: to answer for the child (faith) and promise instruction. Obligations: instruct the child in religious duties if parents neglect or die; be faithful in fulfilling this duty. Ineligibility: (1) non-Catholics (cannot teach the Catholic religion), (2) persons publicly leading bad lives (public sinners), (3) persons ignorant of their religion. A sponsor may stand by proxy (not present) provided someone else holds the child and answers for them. Sponsors contract a spiritual relationship with the godchild; this relationship can affect future marriage (dispensation required to marry a godchild).

rubrics_metrics.name: Baptismal naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on choosing a name at Baptism and its religious purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A saint's name is given to encourage imitation of that saint's virtues and for patronage. Avoid names of enemies of the Church or unbelievers. If no saint's name is chosen, supply one in Confirmation as a middle name. Do not shorten or change a saint's name into meaningless pet names (e.g., Mazie for Mary) because using the correct name honors the saint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may administer Confirmation and exceptional norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary and exceptional ministers for Confirmation and limits on their powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishop is the ordinary minister of Confirmation. In remote regions lacking bishops, the Pope may permit a priest to give Confirmation, but that priest must use holy oil consecrated by a bishop and cannot consecrate oil himself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and ritual of Confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: How the bishop confers Confirmation and the words and gestures used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishop extends his hands over those to be confirmed, prays for the Holy Ghost, and anoints the forehead with holy chrism in the form of a cross. The formula said: "I sign thee with the Sign of the Cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost." The bishop may give a slight blow on the cheek to remind the confirmand to be ready to suffer for Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and preparation to receive Confirmation worthily
rubrics_metrics.description: Spiritual and instructional prerequisites for a proper reception of Confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is necessary to be in the state of grace to receive Confirmation worthily. Persons of an age to learn should know the chief mysteries of the faith, the duties of a Christian, and be instructed in the nature and effects of the Sacrament. Neglecting Confirmation when able to receive it is considered sinful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects and gifts of the Holy Ghost (from Confirmation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spiritual effects bestowed by Confirmation and the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost with their purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects include an increase of sanctifying grace and the strengthening of faith. The seven gifts: wisdom (gives a relish for divine things and directs life to God's glory), understanding (helps one know more clearly the mysteries of faith), counsel (warns of the devil's deceits and dangers to salvation), fortitude (gives courage to do God's will), knowledge (enables discovery of God's will in things), piety (makes one love God as Father and obey Him from love), and fear of the Lord (fills with dread of sin). Each gift's practical effect is described (e.g., counsel warns against people/places dangerous to salvation; fortitude helps act on conscience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beatitudes: virtues to practice and their rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: List and explanation of the Beatitudes as conditions and virtues for Christian life and their promised rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The eight Beatitudes (poor in spirit, meek, those who mourn, hunger and thirst after justice, merciful, clean of heart, peacemakers, those persecuted for justice's sake) are explained with practical meanings and examples (e.g., poor in spirit means not setting heart on riches; peacemakers are children of God and opposed to those who stir dissension). The sermon on the Mount context and rewards (God's grace, future glory) are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve fruits of the Holy Ghost
rubrics_metrics.description: The twelve fruits (charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, long-suffering, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity) and brief meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fruits grow from the gifts of the Holy Ghost. Definitions include: charity (love of God and neighbor), peace (with God, man, and self), benignity (disposition to do good), long-suffering (patience), modesty/continency/chastity (purity in thoughts, words, looks, and actions), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition, purpose, and importance of the Sacrament of Penance
rubrics_metrics.description: Penance is the sacrament by which sins committed after Baptism are forgiven, restoring the soul to God's friendship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penance is necessary because Baptism is conferred once and sins committed after Baptism must be forgiven by another sacrament. The sacrament includes confession, absolution, and penance; it is a means of spiritual counsel, instruction, and reconciliation. The priest acts as God's minister with authority given by Christ to forgive sins. The sacrament is compared to a plank in a shipwreck: essential to be saved after falling into sin.

rubrics_metrics.name: How absolution is given (form and ritual in Penance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The priest prays and pronounces specific words and gestures to absolve sins; the formula and ritual sequence are prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After confession and assignment of penance, the priest prays: "May Almighty God have mercy on you, and, your sins being forgiven, bring you to life everlasting. Amen." Then, raising his right hand, he says: "May the Almighty and merciful Lord grant you pardon, absolution, and remission of your sins. Amen." He continues: "May Our Lord Jesus Christ absolve you, and I, by His authority, absolve you from every bond of excommunication and interdict, as far as I have power and you stand in need. Then I absolve you from your sins, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen." He makes the Sign of the Cross over the penitent and concludes with a prayer invoking the Passion of Our Lord and blessings, then dismisses with "God bless you," "Go in peace," etc. The priest's exercise of this power is validated by Christ's grant to the Apostles (e.g., John 20:23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of confession, role, and conduct of the confessor
rubrics_metrics.description: Confession is confidential; the priest keeps penitent's secrets and gives counsel without expectation of reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whatever is told in the confessional will never be made known to others; the priest is bound to conceal it even at the cost of his life. The priest is not paid for absolution; reports that Catholics pay priests for forgiveness are false. The confessor offers instruction, advice, and encouragement and plays a pastoral role in saving souls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five acts required to receive the Sacrament of Penance worthily
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive Penance worthily a penitent must perform five things: examine conscience, have sorrow, make firm resolution, confess, and accept penance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five acts: (1) Examine your conscience (best method: use the Ten Commandments and review each to recall offenses and times since last confession), (2) Be sorry for your sins (contrition), (3) Make a firm resolution never to offend God again, (4) Confess your sins to the priest, (5) Accept and perform the penance the priest assigns. Pray to the Holy Ghost for light and memory before confession.
